assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the TW average of 12,000-15,000 km. Every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). This drives two things. (1) SERVICING IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: Volvo's interval is 10,000 km OR 12 months, whichever comes first, so at 7,000 km/year the clock always wins and the car gets exactly one annual service and never a mileage-triggered one. Wear items therefore age out rather than wear out: 235/55 R19 tyres (confirmed as the factory size in Volvo TW's own MY26 XC60 sheet, same fitment as the B5) are replaced on rubber age at ~5-6 years, and the 12V AGM battery dies on calendar life. Volvo Taiwan's free scheduled-maintenance programme does NOT apply here: volvomsp.volvocartw.com states in its own footnote that the 4-year/80,000 km free maintenance offer is for 電動車 (BEVs: EX30/EX40/EC40/EX90) only, so this PHEV owner pays for every annual service from year 1. (2) RESALE: every XC60 T8 listing found live on 8891/FindCar carries 19,000-109,000 km, all above this buyer's pace, so comps were normalised UPWARD toward 7,000 km/year before the dealer-retail to private-sale haircut. The uplift used for this car is deliberately small (~0.1% per 1,000 km, roughly a quarter of the 0.375% per 1,000 km measured on the petrol/MHEV XC60) because on a PHEV low mileage does not protect the thing buyers actually worry about: the 18.8 kWh pack degrades on calendar age regardless of km, and in Taiwan a very-low-mileage PHEV is often read as a car whose owner never bothered to charge it. The 0.375%/1,000 km petrol figure was measured independently here from 8891's own 2021 XC60 B5 R-Design cohort (NT$1,300,000 @45,200 km vs NT$989,000 @109,000 km). Tax (牌照稅/燃料費/貨物稅) and insurance are excluded by design throughout.

purchase.source: VERIFIED FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE, NOT FROM A SUMMARY. I downloaded Volvo Taiwan's own MY26 XC60 price/specification sheet (https://www.volvocartw.com/pdf/carsp/XC60.pdf, HTTP 200, 264 KB, 7 pages) and decompressed its PDF text streams directly. The raw stream reads 'XC60, B5 AWD' / 'XC60, T8 AWD plug in Hybrid' with 'Plus : NT$2,390,000', 'Ultra : NT$2,690,000' and 'Ultra : NT$2,990,000', and the sheet carries an 'MY26' version stamp. The same stream confirms 235/55 R19 tyres and the 18.8 kWh battery. CarStuff independently prints the identical three-car range: 'XC60 B5 MHEV Plus AWD：$239 萬元 / XC60 B5 MHEV Ultra AWD：$269 萬元 / XC60 T8 PHEV Ultra AWD：$299 萬元'. list_price is therefore confirmed at NT$2,990,000, 0% deviation from the briefed figure, no correction needed. DISCOUNT: anchored on documented Volvo TW behaviour rather than a guess. CarStuff reports the launch '隨心入主方案' putting the B5 Plus AWD at NT$2,240,000 against a NT$2,390,000 list, i.e. NT$150,000 (6.3%) off, plus a bundled HUD worth NT$60,000. 8891's August 2026 Volvo package gives XC60 buyers 120萬 40期 0利率 plus a free HUD upgrade, and explicitly advises giving up the interest subsidy in exchange for a deeper 純空車現金折扣. NT$180,000 (6.0% of list) is a realistic negotiated cash 空車折讓 on the T8 Ultra: larger in absolute terms than the documented B5 Plus offer, because this is the slowest-moving halo trim in the range, but slightly lower as a percentage, as flagship trims usually are. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from discounts: the government 舊換新 + 貨物稅減徵 subsidy of up to NT$100,000 (conditional on scrapping a 10-year-old car, and it is a tax rebate, which this table excludes by design) and the bundled HUD (an accessory, not cash).
purchase.notes: Full official designation is 'XC60 T8 AWD Plug-in Hybrid Ultra', the MY2026 (second-facelift) car, and it is the only T8 in the current three-car Taiwan XC60 range (B5 Plus AWD / B5 Ultra AWD / T8 Ultra AWD). Powertrain per Volvo TW's own sheet and CarStuff: second-generation PHEV architecture, engine on the front axle plus a rear electric motor forming e-AWD, combined 455 hp / 72.3 kgm, 18.8 kWh lithium pack, up to 86 km of pure-electric range and a 140 km/h EV top speed; the T8 gets the Bowers & Wilkins 15-speaker 1,410 W system where the B5 gets Harman Kardon. onroad_fees of NT$50,000 covers 領牌規費, 代辦服務費 and basic delivery accessories (mats, window film, dashcam) at this price level; it is scaled consistently with the other Volvo records in this table (NT$40,000 at the NT$2,390,000 XC60 B5, NT$45,000 at the NT$2,790,000 V60 T8, NT$65,000 at the NT$3,776,000 XC90 T8). real_cost = 2,990,000 - 180,000 + 50,000 = 2,860,000. Tax and insurance excluded by design.

items.name: 過戶規費 + 代辦服務費
售前整備／美容（內外清潔、拋光鍍膜、小補漆、輪圈整理）

selling_costs.notes: Cost of actually completing a private sale, at the level normal for a 2-3 million TWD European SUV. Pre-sale detailing is the big line: a car at this price will not attract private-buyer money without paint correction and a proper interior clean. One PHEV-specific point that is NOT charged here but is worth knowing: Volvo TW's prepaid 保養服務合約 (VOLVO Plus) is transferable to the next owner, so an unused balance is a genuine selling aid rather than a sunk cost.

value_checkpoints.source: BACKCAST ONE YEAR FROM REAL LISTINGS; NO 1-YEAR-OLD T8 IS CURRENTLY ON THE MARKET, so this is not a directly observed point. The nearest real data is the age-2.1 cohort on 8891: 2024款 Recharge Ultimate T8 AWD at NT$1,950,000 / 19,000 km and NT$1,930,000 / 26,500 km, both against a verified MY2024 list of NT$2,941,000 (FindCar new-car reference table), i.e. 0.663 and 0.656 of list as DEALER RETAIL ASKING. Normalising both to this buyer's mileage gives ~0.665 of list at 2.1 years. Backcasting the fitted curve (0.665 @2.1y, 0.609 @3.1y, 0.520 @4.1y) to 1 year gives ~0.74 of list as dealer retail, consistent with a ~25-point first-year loss, which is normal for a Taiwan luxury PHEV; the shape is cross-checked against the one near-1-year XC60 B5 on FindCar (2024-built / 2025-registered, 11,704 km, asking NT$1,758,000). ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: 0.74 x NT$2,990,000 = NT$2,212,600 dealer retail, then -15% to reach the PRIVATE SALE figure of NT$1,880,000. The 15% haircut is the deep end of the normal 8-15% band, used deliberately because the private buyer pool for a PHEV in Taiwan is much smaller than for the petrol equivalent (the buyer needs somewhere to charge), so a private seller must discount harder and wait longer. dealer_tradein_price is a further -13% below the private figure. This is NOT a copied dealer asking price.

BEST-EVIDENCED POINT ON THE CURVE: three real matched-age XC60 T8 listings, each with a verified original list price. From 8891 and FindCar, the age-3.1 (reg-2023) cohort is 2023款 Recharge Ultimate T8 at NT$1,750,000 / 39,600 km against a MY2023 Ultimate T8 list of NT$2,925,000 (0.598), plus 2024款 Recharge Plus T8 AWD at NT$1,500,000 / 51,000 km and NT$1,530,000 / 42,000 km against a MY2023-24 Plus T8 list of NT$2,555,000-2,571,000 (0.587 and 0.599). Three independent points converging on 0.59-0.60 of list is a strong signal. Normalising to this buyer's 21,000 km gives 0.609 of list as DEALER RETAIL ASKING. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: 0.609 x NT$2,990,000 = NT$1,820,900 dealer retail, then -15% to the PRIVATE SALE figure of NT$1,545,000; dealer_tradein_price is a further -13%. HONEST NOTE ON THE PHEV PENALTY: matched-trim, matched-age, mileage-normalised ASKING prices do not actually show the T8 below the B5 here (T8 0.609 of list vs the 2023 Ultimate B5 AWD at NT$1,359,000 / 65,200 km against a NT$2,612,000 list, normalising to ~0.605). The PHEV penalty in Taiwan is real but it lands on the seller as a deeper private-sale discount and a much longer time on market, not as a lower dealer sticker, which is exactly why the 15% haircut rather than the 8-10% one is applied to this car. Confidence is medium, not high, because these are asking prices, not recorded transactions, and the retail-to-private conversion is modelled.

INTERPOLATED BETWEEN TWO REAL BRACKETS. Lower bracket, real and same model: the age-4.1 XC60 T8 cohort on 8891, 2023款 Recharge T8 AWD Plus at NT$1,299,000 / 51,100 km and 2022款 XC60 T8 PLUS at NT$1,230,000 / 109,000 km, both against a NT$2,555,000 list, which normalise to a tight 0.519-0.520 of list. Upper bracket, real but a sibling model: the age-6.1 XC90 T8 Inscription at NT$1,588,000 / 42,000 km against its NT$3,690,000 list (FindCar new-car table) = 0.430 of list. Interpolating gives ~0.480 of list at exactly 5 years as DEALER RETAIL ASKING. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: 0.480 x NT$2,990,000 = NT$1,435,200 dealer retail, then -15% to the PRIVATE SALE figure of NT$1,220,000; dealer_tradein_price a further -13%. Year 5 is where the PHEV genuinely falls behind the mild-hybrid: this is the first checkpoint fully outside the 3-year factory warranty, and the pack is now old enough that buyers start pricing battery-health uncertainty. Confidence medium: the year-5 value is bracketed on both sides by real listings, but the upper bracket is a different model, so the shape between them is modelled.

EXTRAPOLATED BEYOND ALL XC60 T8 DATA. The oldest XC60 T8 on the Taiwan market today is the reg-2020 T8 Inscription (NT$1,188,000 / 63,000 km on 8891), only ~6 years old, and its original list price could not be verified, so it is used for shape only and not as a ratio. The anchor used instead is the oldest Volvo PHEV with a verifiable denominator: the age-6.1 XC90 T8 Inscription at NT$1,588,000 / 42,000 km against a NT$3,690,000 list = 0.430 of list. Extending the observed ~4.5 points/year decay to 7 years gives ~0.390, and this is cut to 0.375 of list because year 7 sits directly under the battery cliff: Volvo's high-voltage battery warranty is 8 years / 160,000 km, so a 7-year-old car is sold with roughly one year of pack cover left and buyers discount that explicitly. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: 0.375 x NT$2,990,000 = NT$1,121,250 dealer retail, then -15% to the PRIVATE SALE figure of NT$950,000; dealer_tradein_price a further -13%. Confidence low: no XC60 T8 of this age exists to check against, and the decay rate past year 6 is inferred from a larger, more expensive sibling model.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREVIOUS-GENERATION XC60, WITH AN EXPLICIT CORRECTION FOR THE FACT THAT NO 10-YEAR-OLD XC60 T8 CAN EXIST. Stating the gap plainly: the T8 was only introduced on the second-generation XC60, which reached Taiwan in 2018, so the oldest XC60 T8 in the country is about 8 years old; and the older Volvo PHEV, the XC90 T8, returned no 2016-2017 listings at all in this search. There is therefore no real 10-year Volvo PHEV transaction data in Taiwan, and none is invented here. METHOD ACTUALLY USED, exactly as required: take the real used prices of the PREVIOUS-GENERATION XC60 at that age, express them as a retention ratio of that car's own original list price, then apply the ratio to this car's real_cost. From 8891, the first-generation XC60 T5 R-Design reg-2015 sells at NT$358,000 / 126,400 km against its NT$2,210,000 MY2015 list (FindCar historical new-car table) = 0.162 of list at ~11 years; the reg-2014 T5 R-Design at NT$258,000 / 162,000 km against NT$2,115,000 = 0.122 at ~12 years. Normalising the 11-year car to 70,000 km (uplift capped at +20%, the convention used elsewhere in this table) gives ~0.194, and at 10 years rather than 11 the petrol previous generation sits at ~0.21 of list as dealer retail asking. That chain reproduces the XC60 B5 record's own 10-year figure to within about 4%, which is the main check that the method is not drifting. PHEV PENALTY APPLIED ON TOP: 0.21 is cut by 20% relative, to 0.168 of list, because by year 10 the high-voltage pack is two years out of warranty and a pack replacement costs a large fraction of what the whole car is then worth, which is the single biggest thing a Taiwanese buyer of a 10-year-old PHEV is pricing. 0.168 x NT$2,990,000 = NT$502,320 dealer retail, then -15% to the PRIVATE SALE figure of NT$430,000; dealer_tradein_price a further -13%. Note the crossover this produces: in absolute money this car finally falls BELOW the XC60 B5 at year 10 (NT$430,000 vs NT$450,000) despite having cost NT$600,000 more new. That is deliberate and is the point of the record: the battery risk eventually overwhelms the higher starting price. Confidence low, and it should be treated as an ordering signal, not a number to plan around.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Volvo's service interval is 10,000 km OR 12 months, whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/year the clock always wins, so this car receives exactly one time-triggered annual service every year and never reaches a mileage-triggered one; period_cost below is therefore counted as (number of years in the window) x (one annual service) plus whatever consumables age out inside that window. NO FREE MAINTENANCE APPLIES TO THIS CAR. Volvo Taiwan does run a free scheduled-maintenance programme, but its own service-planning site states in the footnote that '台灣市場Volvo電動車享有4年或8萬公里免費保養專案' - it is for the BEVs (EX30 / EX40 / EC40 / EX90), not for the T8 PHEV. The T8 owner pays from the first service. What IS available is the prepaid VOLVO Plus 保養服務合約, a one-off prepayment covering five scheduled services, which locks in today's prices and is transferable to the next owner; it changes when the money is spent, not how much, so it is not modelled separately. WARRANTY BOUNDARIES THAT SHAPE THE CURVE: 3-year unlimited-mileage vehicle warranty (so years 1-3 carry servicing cost but no repair risk), and 8-year / 160,000 km high-voltage battery warranty, which at 7,000 km/year expires on the CALENDAR at year 8 - squarely inside the 7-10 year window, which is why that period carries a high-voltage allowance rather than the earlier ones. PHEV-SPECIFIC COST ITEMS not present on the B5: a second coolant circuit for the battery on top of the engine circuit, high-voltage system inspection at the later services, and a 12V battery that lives a harder life than on a conventional car. Working the other way, regenerative braking means the friction pads last much longer than on a pure combustion car - at this mileage the front discs are more likely to be condemned for surface corrosion from light use than the pads are for wear. Anchor for the price of one annual service: a PTT owner receipt for an XC60 shows NT$7,644 for the 10,000 km service (工資 1,575 + 機油芯 756 + 機油 4,998 + 清潔劑 315) and NT$9,514 for the 20,000 km service (工資 2,678 + 機油芯 767 + 機油 4,998 + 煞車油 756 + 清潔劑 315), with the cabin filter absorbed into the labour. Those are older prices on a petrol car; NT$12,000-16,000 per annual service is used here for a 2026 T8, rising with age as labour rates climb and the high-voltage inspection is added.

checkpoints.source: Priced from the PTT XC60 owner receipt (NT$7,644 for a 10,000 km service at 2020 prices, itemised down to the oil filter) uprated to 2026 labour and parts rates and to the T8's more involved service, which adds a high-voltage system check the B5 does not have. Cross-checked for consistency against the other Volvo records in this table at the same age (XC60 B5 NT$10,000, V60 T8 NT$11,000, XC90 T8 NT$15,000); the XC60 T8 sitting just above the V60 T8 and well below the larger XC90 T8 is the expected ordering. Confirmed against volvomsp.volvocartw.com that no free-maintenance programme offsets this, because that offer is BEV-only.

煞車油更換（Volvo 建議 2 年一次，時間到期非里程到期）

checkpoints.source: Two annual services at the PTT-derived rate plus the time-based brake-fluid change (the owner receipt shows 煞車油 756 as a parts line at the second service, with labour absorbed) and cabin filters, whose Volvo parts price the same thread puts at NT$3,014 excluding labour. Still inside the 3-year unlimited-mileage warranty, so no repair reserve is carried. Consistent with the XC60 B5 record's NT$27,000 for the same window, with the T8 slightly higher for the extra high-voltage checks.

major_items: 2 次年度定期保養（第 4、5 年），保固已於第 3 年結束，全額自費
第一套輪胎更換 235/55 R19 四條（約 44,000）— 低里程下是橡膠老化到期，不是磨耗到底
12V AGM 啟動電池（PHEV 對 12V 電瓶負擔重，4-5 年壽命，約 9,000）

煞車油、冷氣濾網 x2、四輪定位
首次高壓系統與電池健康度檢測
checkpoints.source: Tyre size 235/55 R19 taken from Volvo TW's own MY26 XC60 specification sheet, priced at the same ~NT$44,000 fitted as the XC60 B5 record, which shares the exact fitment. This is the first window fully outside the 3-year warranty, so services are at full dealer rate. Consistent with the sibling records (XC60 B5 NT$92,000, V60 T8 NT$95,000) with the T8 carrying more because of the 12V battery's harder life on a PHEV and the first battery-health diagnostic. Confidence low: no XC60 T8 has yet been through this window in Taiwan at this mileage, so the consumable timing is inferred from the platform rather than observed on this exact car.

major_items: 2 次年度定期保養（第 6、7 年），每次約 15,000
火星塞更換 — T8 的 2.0L 同時渦輪加機械增壓，作業較單純渦輪繁複（約 14,000）
冷卻液更換：引擎迴路與高壓電池獨立冷卻迴路兩套（PHEV 專屬，約 9,000）
高壓系統詳細檢測與電池健康度報告（保固將於第 8 年到期前的關鍵檢查）
後煞車來令片與碟盤（約 16,000）
煞車油、冷氣濾網 x2、雨刷
過保修繕準備金約 35,000：水泵浦／節溫器、點火線圈、電子式冷卻水泵、懸吊橡膠襯套與連桿、感知器
checkpoints.source: This is the window the briefing flags for extra high-voltage inspection cost, and it is priced that way: the PHEV-only second coolant circuit and the pre-expiry battery health assessment are both charged here, on top of the spark plugs that the T8's twin-charged (turbo plus supercharger) 2.0L needs on a calendar trigger at this mileage. Out-of-warranty repair reserve is carried from year 4 onward. Benchmarked against the V60 T8 record (NT$105,000, identical powertrain, smaller car and smaller brakes) and the XC90 T8 (NT$130,000, larger and air-sprung); NT$115,000 for the XC60 T8 sits correctly between them. Confidence low: a reserve for unscheduled out-of-warranty repair is a probability-weighted figure, not a quotation.

major_items: 3 次年度定期保養（第 8、9、10 年），每次約 17,000
第二套輪胎 235/55 R19（約 48,000）— 同樣是老化到期
第二顆 12V AGM 電池（約 10,000）
Aisin 8AT 變速箱油更換（時間到期，約 17,000）
前後碟盤更換與來令片（約 26,000）
煞車油 x2、冷卻液（含高壓電池迴路）、冷氣濾網
高壓電池風險準備金約 60,000 — 8 年／160,000 km 保固在此區間內以「時間」到期（7,000 km/年永遠跑不到里程上限），整包更換是六位數，此為機率加權的模組級維修準備，不是整包更換價
過保修繕準備金約 40,000：水泵浦、A/C 壓縮機、引擎腳、避震器總成、電子模組與感知器
checkpoints.source: The defining cost of this window is that the high-voltage battery warranty expires on the CALENDAR at year 8 for this driver: at 7,000 km/year the car reaches only ~56,000 km by then, nowhere near the 160,000 km limit, so the time limit is what binds and the last two years are uncovered. The NT$60,000 line is a probability-weighted allowance for module-level repair, not the cost of a full pack, which would be far higher; it is the single largest reason this record's year 7-10 maintenance exceeds the XC60 B5's. Benchmarked against the V60 T8 (NT$200,000, same powertrain, smaller consumables) and the XC90 T8 (NT$300,000, bigger tyres, air suspension); NT$235,000 sits between them as expected. Confidence low: no XC60 T8 in Taiwan has reached 10 years, so this is a constructed bill of materials, not observed spend.

sources.note: Sibling-PHEV data used to shape the curve past year 5, where no XC60 T8 exists: XC90 T8 Inscription original lists of NT$3,690,000 (2020/2021) and NT$3,760,000-3,776,000 (2023/2024). Also confirms no 2016-2017 XC90 T8 is currently listed, which is why no true 10-year Volvo PHEV data point exists.

sources.name: 8891 中古車 — Volvo XC90 二手車listings
sources.note: Supplied the two real XC90 T8 points: reg-2020 T8 Inscription NT$1,588,000 / 42,000 km (age 6.1) and reg-2022 Recharge T8 Inscription NT$1,888,000 / 54,000 km (age 4.1). The age-6.1 point is the oldest Volvo PHEV in Taiwan with a verifiable original list price and is the anchor for years 7 and 10.

sources.name: Volvo Cars Taiwan — 保養服務規劃 (official scheduled-maintenance planner)
sources.note: DECIDES THE FREE-MAINTENANCE QUESTION. Its own footnote reads '台灣市場Volvo電動車享有4年或8萬公里免費保養專案', i.e. the free 4-year/80,000 km programme covers BEVs only. It does NOT cover this T8 PHEV, so every annual service is charged from year 1.

sources.name: PTT car 板 — [心得] Volvo XC60 2萬KM保養分享
sources.note: Real itemised owner receipts for an XC60: 10,000 km service NT$7,644 (工資 1,575 / 機油芯 756 / 機油 4,998 / 清潔劑 315) and 20,000 km service NT$9,514 (工資 2,678 / 機油芯 767 / 機油 4,998 / 煞車油 756 / 清潔劑 315), plus a NT$3,014 parts price for the cabin filter. This is the base rate the maintenance checkpoints are uprated from.

sources.name: dacota.tw — VOLVO Plus 保養服務合約
sources.note: Describes the prepaid maintenance contract: a one-off prepayment covering five scheduled services over five years, transferable to the next owner. Relevant because it shifts when maintenance money is spent and adds a small resale advantage, but does not reduce the total, so it is noted rather than modelled.
